english: Why, guest, do you follow my sheep? I saw a wolf on the path. I protect you. I do not fear wolves; my dog is big. Your dog lies under the tree. I will come home and carry your lamb. What is your name, guest? I am Good-horse. What is your name? Good-mind. Our house is near; come.

Kinsman, you forgot my feast. Why did you not come? I did not want that. A wolf went among the sheep at night. Did it kill anything? It killed nothing; my goatherd drove it away. Now I am not angry. Does your arm hurt? My arm hurts. Come and sit with me. I will wash your arm.

How did you win my grandmother? Her brothers' horses are swift. I yoked my two horses and (raced) against them. You won? I won; my horses are swifter than the grandfathers'. And my grandmother? She smiled and spoke. Now (win) me. What did you put? Every year in the evenings I sang your grandmother a song and still I sing.

Why do you not eat now? Your bowl is full. I am not hungry. Sleep does not come to me. Did a god strike you? A girl struck me with her eyes. Which girl? Good-fame's sister. She is upright. Now eat, and I will speak to her mother soon. Now I eat.

Why do you blush, Good-fame? The sun burns. The sun? Evening has come. Now love burns me. I know. Why do you tremble? I am not a wolf. You are not a wolf; I am a lamb. Now, lamb, come and walk with me to the spring.

Why are you awake early? The others sleep. Sleep fled from me. I remember a woman's eyes. Whose eyes? The goose-girl's. She drives the geese to the meadow early. Now go to the meadow early and speak to her. What shall I say? Say: your geese are white and you are whiter than them. At dawn I shall speak.
